issue.title: [Bug] Daily check-in goes out through the global proxy, not the account's own (accountProxies ignored on the whole check-in path)
issue.body:
**The behavior**

With `proxy` / `accountProxies` set per account (the setting #1663 and #237 added), **every daily check-in goes out through the global proxy**, not the account's own. Model requests, allowance reads and token renewals all follow the account; the check-in alone does not.

This matters more than it looks. A check-in is a signed, authenticated call made once a day per account, and it lands on the vendor's `/signin/claim` — one of the endpoints account-risk systems watch for "same account seen from a new place". So the one path that ignores the account's route is the one that most visibly breaks the per-account separation `accountProxies` exists to give.

**Where it comes from**

The check-in loop never carries an account choice in its ctx. `gateway.go:475` starts it with the server's own ctx:

```go
go provider.KeepMiniMaxCheckedIn(ctx)   // and the same for workbuddy, trae, qoder, plugins
```

and nothing between there and the vendor call adds one (`grep` for `ViaLogin|ProxyOfLogin|netproxy.With` across `checkin.go`, `plugin_checkin.go`, `minimax_checkin.go`, `qoder_checkin.go`, `trae_checkin.go`, `workbuddy_checkin.go` finds none). So `netproxy.Choice(ctx)` is empty all the way down and `netproxy` falls back to the global proxy.

Two shapes, same hole:

- **A plugin that checks in itself** (`plugin_checkin.go:67`): `plugin.AccountCheckin(ctx, id, acct)` → `providers.go:984` sends `"proxy": proxyOf(ctx)` → `""` → the host's `checkinOf` runs with no proxy of its own and takes the global one.
- **magpie's own check-in through a plugin's fetch** (`minimax_checkin.go:307`, `qoder_checkin.go:279`, `trae_checkin.go:243`, `workbuddy_checkin.go:443`): `plugin.Fetch(req.Context(), …)` with `FetchRequest.Proxy` unset, so `Fetch` (`host.go:1496`) sets it from `proxyOf(ctx)` — again `""`.

**Why this is not the same as #1938**

#1938 was the signed-in Claude account's `/usage` read taking the wrong route, and it was fixed in 15105161e by identifying the signed-in account from its sign-in. That was one path. This is the background check-in loop, which has no account dimension in its signature at all — `checkinAcct.do` is `func(context.Context) WorkBuddyCheckin`, with the account closed over rather than passed.

For contrast, the allowance read does it right and is two lines away in spirit (`login_usage.go:314`):

```go
func loginQuota(ctx context.Context, l Login) SubscriptionQuota {
	ctx = ViaLogin(ctx, loginProvider(l), l.User) // asked through the account's own proxy
```

**How I found it**

Debugging why a pool of accounts bound to individual exits still showed one account's daily check-in on a different IP than its requests. The checks: `magpie quota` (allowance) → the account's proxy as expected; a model request → the account's proxy; the daily check-in → the global proxy's egress IP.

**Suggested direction**

Carry the account's choice into the ctx where the account is known, as `loginQuota` does. Each `checkinAcct` already closes over its login, so the wrap can happen when the runner is built (`a.do(ctx)` becomes `a.do(ViaLogin(ctx, card, user))`) — one place per vendor rather than per call site. `pluginCheckinAcct` has the same shape (`plugin_checkin.go:58-70`), where the `plugin` id and `l.User` are both in hand.

Note the plugin-host side already supports this: `AccountCheckin` passes `proxy` through, `host.js:1889` runs `checkin` inside `via.run(proxy ?? "", …)`, and the plugin's `accountCall` inherits it. Only the Go side never fills it in.

**Version**

magpie 0.1.1280 on Windows; also true of `main` as of 2026-10-18 — `plugin_checkin.go`, `checkin.go`, `minimax_checkin.go` were fetched from `main` and all still call with the bare ctx.

comments.body:
Delivered on `fix/checkin-account-proxy` ([69eaf094](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/69eaf094), skygunner's fork, on upstream/main 42976f9a), following the direction you laid out: each runner builder wraps its accounts' `do` with `CheckinVia(provider, user, do)` — `ViaLogin` into the ctx, the same wrap `loginQuota` gives the allowance read — so the check-in runs through the proxy the account's own requests and reads take. All five paths are wired: magpie's own Trae CN, MiniMax, Qoder and WorkBuddy check-ins, and the plugins' through `AccountCheckin`, whose host side already read the proxy from the ctx (`via.run(proxy ?? "")`) — only the Go side never filled it in.

Semantics: an account with no proxy of its own follows its provider's proxy, never another account's; a provider without proxies leaves the choice empty, as any other path does when nothing is set. User-set proxies are only read, never overridden.

Red before: `TestCheckinViaCarriesTheAccountsProxy` — the wrap did not exist, and with a provider on a global proxy and one account (hu) on its own exit, the check-in ran on the global (your shape: the check-in's egress IP differing from the account's requests). After, hu runs on `http://hu-exit.example:8080`, an account without its own follows the provider's, and a provider without proxies leaves it empty.

Run: `go test ./internal/provider -count=1` (ok, 42 s), gofmt, go vet, windows/amd64 and darwin/arm64 builds. One boundary, as you noted yourself would matter: not pressed against a real vendor — the test's proxies are names on an isolated providers.json, and no real check-in was sent.

Fixed in 69626580b, in v0.1.1797.

Every check-in now goes through the account's own proxy, or the provider's if the account has none. Before this, they all went through the global proxy. It's done once, where `checkiner` runs an account (`checkin.go`: `a.do(ViaLogin(ctx, a.provider, a.User))`), so it covers a plugin's own check-in (`plugin.AccountCheckin`) and magpie's Trae CN, MiniMax, Qoder and WorkBuddy check-ins through `plugin.Fetch`, for the loop and for a press. This is the direction the issue laid out (and skygunner's fork wired per runner).

The same commit fixes a related path: `Provider.Origin` asked the plugin's loader with the bare ctx, before WorkBuddy's search and draw paths added the account's proxy. It now goes through `p.Via(ctx)`. I read the other plugin-host entries (sign-in, the move's Check, usage, model lists, the gateway's fetch), and each already sends the proxy.

Reported on Discord by zRain (Windows, Loomy plugin 0.1.4): the provider was set to direct and the global proxy was a residential entry, so balance reads worked but check-ins failed with ECONNRESET.

Test: `TestPluginCheckinGoesThroughItsProxy`. The provider is set to direct, one account has its own proxy, and the global proxy is a recorder. Over the loop and then a press, the global proxy must never be asked, and the account's proxy must carry its check-in. It goes red when the old `a.do(ctx)` is put back, and fails the same way the report did: the global proxy was asked for both accounts. The full `go test -tags nogui ./...` suite passed on macOS.

Not tried: a real Loomy check-in on Windows. Leaving this open for the reporter to confirm.

issue.title: [feat] 多账号一键自动签到（Trae CN / WorkBuddy 国内版），并在签到后直接反代使用

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 背景

Magpie 已经有签到能力（warmups / daily check-in），但在真实「薅羊毛」场景里还差最后一公里：**多账号批量签到**、以及**签到拿到的额度能立刻通过反代用起来**。

## 期望能力

### 1. 多账号一键签到

- **Trae（CN）**：希望支持多个账号自动签到，每个账号每日自动领 100 积分。
- **WorkBuddy 国内版**：希望支持多个账号自动签到。
- 交互上希望能有一个入口（GUI 或插件），对同一 provider 下的**所有账号一键批量签到**，而不是逐个手动点。

### 2. 签到完之后直接反代出来使用

- 签到拿到额度后，同一账号应当能被 Magpie 直接反代给下游 agent（Codex / Claude Code / Trae / WorkBuddy 等）使用，即「签到 → 拿额度 → 反代消费」是一条完整链路。
- 现状签到与代理更像两条独立链路（参见 #2777：签到走的是全局代理而不是账号自己的代理）。希望签到完成后，额度能立即在反代中生效。

## 相关 issue

- #2014 希望能支持 trae、traecn、qoder cn 等
- #2777 [Bug] Daily check-in goes out through the global proxy, not the account's own (accountProxies ignored on the whole check-in path)
- #2816 WorkBuddy AI: distinguish activity rewards from automatic check-in
- #2812 warmups plugin: automatic daily check-in never runs (no check-in state files or logs)
- #1705 [Trae CN 签到] 可以抄 DSH 插件 dsh-connect-trae 的做法：读本机真实 Trae 客户端的设备身份
- #821 trae cn 签到失败

（如果其中某条已经覆盖了「多账号批量」的部分，我可以把用例和账号数量补充到对应 issue 里，避免重复跟踪。）

## 补充

我这边有多个 Trae 账号和多个 WorkBuddy 国内账号可以配合测试，也可以在需要时提供签到接口的抓包样本。

issue.title: Codex app-server is restarted mid-turn: 512 KiB session tail misses task_started, and route includes a catalog magpie doesn't own

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**Version:** v0.1.1845 (05ed578), macOS arm64, official release. The same code is still on main at 4534561f6 (`sessionTurnTail`, and `codexAppRoute` hashing the `model_catalog_json` file).

**What happens.** `KeepCodexAppOnItsProvider` ends the Codex desktop app's own app-server with SIGTERM while a long turn is still running. The app reconnects with `resumedCurrentConversation=false` and the turn stops. Captured with `eslogger signal`: sender `magpie tray`, target the app's bundled `codex` app-server.

**Why the turn counts as idle.** `sessionTurnOpen` (`internal/provider/codex_app_server.go`) reads only the last `sessionTurnTail = 512 << 10` bytes of the rollout. In a long turn the `task_started` record is further back than that and no `task_complete`/`turn_aborted` follows, so `started == ended == -1` and the turn is reported closed. Replaying the rollout up to the signal time: the whole file says a turn is open, the 512 KiB tail says it isn't.

**Why the route changed at all.** Codex's `model_provider` was `openai`, not magpie. `codexAppRoute` (`internal/agent/agents.go`) still hashes the file `model_catalog_json` points to. Here a separate local tool writes that catalog and rewrote it on every Codex models-cache refresh (only `fetched_at` differed), so magpie saw a new route every few minutes and restarted the app-server repeatedly (30+ generations in one day).

**Suggestions.**
1. When the tail has neither marker, read further back (or scan the whole file, or keep a per-file offset of the last lifecycle record) instead of treating it as closed; a file that can't be decided counts as open, as the comment already says for unreadable files.
2. Only include `model_catalog_json`'s content in the route when magpie wrote that catalog or is Codex's provider.
3. Optionally, a setting to turn off the automatic app-server restart.

**Workaround used:** make the third-party catalog writer skip identical rewrites.

issue.title: TestPluginCheckinGoesThroughItsProxy fails under load: one minute's ctx is spent before the press (fix on a fork branch)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
A fix for this is on the branch `pr/checkin-test-step-minute` of my fork, one commit on origin/main eff7f9f6 (013c5cb1), ready to merge as it is:

https://github.com/qiqll/magpie/compare/main...pr/checkin-test-step-minute  (branch: https://github.com/qiqll/magpie/tree/pr/checkin-test-step-minute)

PRs are open to collaborators only (docs/contributors.md), so I'm filing it here.

## Summary

`TestPluginCheckinGoesThroughItsProxy` (internal/provider, from 69626580, #2777) fails under a full run on a busy machine:

```
--- FAIL: TestPluginCheckinGoesThroughItsProxy (62.02s)
    plugin_checkin_proxy_test.go:131: a press: the account with its own proxy: {... Outcome:failed ... Msg:context deadline exceeded ...}
    plugin_checkin_proxy_test.go:133: a press: the account's proxy was asked ["http://vendor.invalid/checkin/ck-own"]
```

One minute's ctx covers the whole test: the host's start, the plugin's add, two sign-ins, the loop's check-in and a press. Under load the steps before the press spend most of it, and the press fails on the deadline, not on its proxy. Alone the test passes in 6 to 9s.

## What changed

- `minuteEach(t)` in plugin_checkin_test.go gives each step a minute of its own (cancelled at the test's cleanup).
- TestPluginCheckinGoesThroughItsProxy uses it, and so do the eight places in plugin_checkin_test.go that shared one minute (or two, in TestPluginCheckinAsksAgainAtUntil's subtests) over several steps the same way.
- Test files only; no code under test changes.

## How it was verified (head 013c5cb1, base origin/main eff7f9f6)

- Reproduced by injecting `time.Sleep(58 * time.Second)` after the sign-ins: on main, red exactly as above (62.03s); with the fix, green (67.6s). A 50s injection still passes on main, so the deadline is what the press ran into.
- `go test -count=3 -run 'PluginCheckin|LoginCheckins' ./internal/provider`: ok.
- `go test -count=1 -timeout 45m ./internal/provider`: ok (160s, on the fork's tree with the same change).
- gofmt -l internal/provider: nothing. go vet darwin, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui`, `GOOS=windows go vet` on internal/provider: clean.

## Not tried

Linux and Windows runs (vet only); the full `go test ./...` suite.
